title: The Invention of the Zipper
summary: The story of how an unreliable hook fastener called the clasp locker was redesigned into the modern zipper, replacing slow buttons on boots, bags, and eventually almost all clothing.
poll: The zipper, a small and simple fastener, changed daily life more than most people realize.

versions.title: The Invention of the Zipper
versions.text:
Long ago, there was no zipper. People used buttons. Buttons took time. Each one went in a hole by hand.

A man made a new thing. His name was Whitcomb Judson. It had small hooks. The hooks could lock.

It did not work well. It got stuck a lot. But it gave others an idea. The idea was good.

A man named Gideon Sundback had a plan. He made it better. He used tiny metal teeth. The teeth could lock. They locked well. A small slide moved up and down the teeth.

At first, it went on boots. It went on small bags too. Workers liked how fast it let them fasten things.

Later, a firm used it on boots. They gave it a new name. The name was zipper. The name came from its zip sound.

Soon, people wanted zippers on coats. They wanted them on bags too. Today, zippers are used all over the world.

versions.title: The Invention of the Zipper
versions.text:
Long ago, there was no zipper. People used small buttons on their clothes. Buttons took time to fasten. Each tiny button went through a small hole. People did this one at a time.

A man made a new fastener. The year was 1893. His name was Whitcomb Judson. It had small hooks. The hooks locked along a track. A small slide moved the hooks. People called it a clasp locker.

Sadly, it did not work very well. It got stuck a lot. It popped open too. Still, it gave other inventors a good idea.

A man had a better plan. The year was 1913. His name was Gideon Sundback. He used tiny metal teeth. The teeth locked well. They worked much better than the old hooks.

At first, makers put the new fastener on boots. They put it on small bags too. Workers loved it. It was fast for fastening things.

Later, a shoe firm put it on rubber boots. They gave it a catchy new name: zipper. The name came from its zip sound.

Soon, people wanted zippers on coats. They wanted them on bags and pants too. Today, zippers are used in most countries.

versions.title: The Invention of the Zipper
versions.text:
Long ago, people used small buttons to close their clothing. Buttons took a long time to fasten. Each tiny button had to go through a small hole. People did this one at a time. Their fingers often got cold.

In 1893, a man made a new kind of fastener. His name was Whitcomb Judson. It had small metal hooks. The hooks locked along a track. A small slide pulled the hooks shut. People at the time called it a clasp locker.

Sadly, it did not work very well. It often jammed. It also popped open at bad times. Still, it gave other inventors a good idea to improve on.

In 1913, a man made the design much better. His name was Gideon Sundback. He used tiny metal teeth instead of the old hooks. These teeth locked together far more smoothly than before.

At first, makers used the new fastener mostly on rubber boots. They also used it on tobacco pouches. These items needed to hold up to daily wear. Workers quickly loved how fast it let them fasten things.

Later, a shoe company put the better fastener on a new line of boots. They gave it a catchy name: zipper. The fun name came from the quick zip sound the slide made.

Soon, people everywhere wanted zippers on coats and bags. They wanted them on pants too. Today, zippers are made and used in almost every country.

versions.title: The Invention of the Zipper
versions.text:
Long ago, people used small buttons to close their clothing. Buttons took a long time to fasten properly. Each tiny button had to go through a small, tight hole. People did this one at a time. Their fingers often got cold.

In 1893, a man made a new kind of fastener. His name was Whitcomb Judson. It had small metal hooks that locked along a sliding track. A small slide guided the hooks. People at the time called this odd device a clasp locker.

Sadly, the clasp locker did not work very well in daily life. It jammed a lot. It also popped open at bad moments. This upset anyone who tried wearing it. Still, it gave other curious inventors a good idea worth improving.

In 1913, a man made the whole design much better. His name was Gideon Sundback. He replaced Judson's hooks with tiny, matching metal teeth. He spaced them evenly on both sides. These teeth locked together far more smoothly than before.

At first, makers used the new fastener mostly on rubber boots. They also used it on tobacco pouches. These items got daily use and rough handling. Workers quickly loved how fast it let them open and close things without fumbling.

Later, a shoe company put the better fastener on a popular new line of boots. They gave it a catchy name: zipper. The fun name came straight from the quick zip sound the sliding part made.

Soon, people everywhere wanted zippers sewn onto coats and bags. They wanted them on pants too. Today, zippers are made by the billions. They are used in almost every country.

versions.title: The Invention of the Zipper
versions.text:
For a long time, people used buttons to close their clothes and bags. Buttons took a long time to fasten. Each tiny button had to go through a small hole, one at a time.

In 1893, a man named Whitcomb Judson showed off a new fastener at a fair in Chicago. It had small metal hooks that locked along a track. A tiny slide moved up and down to open and close it. People called this strange device a clasp locker.

Sadly, it did not work very well once people tried wearing it every day. It jammed a lot, or it popped open at bad times. Even so, it gave other inventors a good idea to improve.

In 1913, an engineer named Gideon Sundback finally redesigned the whole thing. He swapped the hooks for tiny metal teeth, spaced evenly on both sides. These teeth locked together far more smoothly than Judson's clumsy hooks ever had.

At first, makers put the improved fastener on rubber boots and small tobacco pouches, items that got rough daily use. Workers quickly liked how fast it let them open and close things, instead of fumbling with buttons.

Later, a company named B.F. Goodrich put the fastener on a new line of rubber boots and gave it a catchy name: zipper. The playful name came from the quick zip sound the slide made.

Within a few decades, people everywhere wanted zippers on jackets, bags, and pants too, and the fastener quickly became popular. Today, factories make zippers by the billions, and they are used in nearly every country.

MID.modelAnswer: Whitcomb Judson invented the clasp locker in 1893, but its hooks often jammed or popped open, so people did not trust it. Gideon Sundback improved the design in 1913 by using tiny matching teeth instead of hooks, which locked together much more smoothly. Because the new fastener worked so well, companies first put it on boots, and it soon became popular on jackets and bags too.

HIGH.modelAnswer: Although Whitcomb Judson had already patented the basic idea of a sliding fastener, his hooked mechanism frequently failed, interlocking unevenly and popping open under normal use. Gideon Sundback's innovation was replacing those hooks with tiny, identical teeth that interlocked consistently and securely along the textile edge, which made the fastener reliable enough for everyday products. This single improvement in mechanism transformed the zipper from a curious failure into one of the most common fasteners used in clothing and textiles worldwide.
